chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Musa from Zurara who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sets out on a journey he intends, and the time enters while he has exited the town by two farsakhs, so they prayed, and some of them returned for his need, then the departure was not completed for him; what should he do regarding the prayer? He said, 'His prayer is complete and he does not repeat it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler who prays after leaving the city but then returns before fully departing?
ai.summary: This narration from Zurara highlights the principle of ease (yusr) in travel jurisprudence, establishing that once a traveler has exited the city limits and performed the shortened prayer, their status is fixed even if they return or delay before fully departing. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the physical act of leaving the urban boundary triggers the ruling of qasr, preventing unnecessary repetition of prayer for minor changes in travel status.
